pr_title: Unify editor icon palette, fix up some inconsistent icons, theme usage
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57129. Part of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56790.

So I've decided to faint two pokemons with one move. The issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56790 put the spotlight on inconsistencies with how editor's SVG icons are created and saved. I've used this opportunity to fix not only scaling issues, but also a bunch of other problems. For example, the breakpoint icon was not only too big, but also malformed (it's supposed to have two discs!). Several icons weren't optimized. Some were hiding their colors in the `style` attribute instead of individual SVG attributes for fill or stroke color.

![godot windows tools 64_2022-01-28_16-15-03](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/151594905-990e5497-de4a-4e88-aff2-b536d78afb42.png)


This was important to start addressing https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57129. I've tried to reduce the number of used colors as much as possible, but there are still a lot of niche colors that we cannot work around. So the conversion table had to be extended as well. I've picked colors without looking too much into how well they work, because that would take an enormous amount of time. They should be sensible, but I'm open to correct the base colors and converted colors in this or future PRs.

![godot windows tools 64_2022-01-28_19-29-28](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/151594920-71720e9b-045c-4a93-a23f-8be5c6ea8903.png)

I've also stored the colors that we don't want to convert, simply for completeness. As described in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57129, we should want to add some sort of CI test/build task to validate the structure of SVGs to avoid aforementioned problems. As such, the conversion table acts as a natural start for tracking our complete panel, so that colors can be validated against it in an organized manner. Refer to my comment https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56790#issuecomment-1024363712 for a bit more details on the matter.

![godot windows tools 64_2022-01-28_19-54-08](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/151594934-bf920dae-ef67-4203-a27f-6d48f98a82dd.png)

-----

While updating icons, I've also noticed a few occasions of icons not working well for the light theme. Part of that were aforementioned issues, but in case of the path and curve editors it was just bad code, so I've fixed it in a dedicated commit. I could've made it a separate PR, but without the rest of these changes, I don't think you can test it.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11782833/151595042-d93c72a7-4fa0-4fe2-a5c6-63cba03ca905.png)

-----

PS. Commits are separate for obvious reasons, they tackle different things and it should be clearer this way. They are still valid independently, but build upon each other.
pr_comments: I've moved around some of those error/warning/success, red/orange/green colors. Apparently, the old success color was not in use, same as the old error color (which was the only thing I fixed initially). So I've gone ahead and reduced the palette further, making sure those replacements actually get applied.

issue_context.title: [4.0] Certain icons are shrunken (SVG scale not taken into account)
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0-dev (6a3ff8f), 4.0-alpha1

### System information

Manjaro Linux 21.2.2

### Issue description

I found a few icons that are shrunken down compared to other ones.
One is the ruler tool and the others are the NavigationAgent and NavigationObstacle nodes.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47503977/150822829-7cb34e23-560c-4fca-b08d-541c88229e29.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47503977/150822931-488ee651-f6b0-4835-bc66-76649ecc2420.png)


### Steps to reproduce

Look for the icons on the latest commit or alpha1.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
And some icons are too big:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/150851828-d6f7ab73-1d08-44ea-b7dd-11597abfccc2.png)

> And some icons are too big:

> 
> 

Pretty sure, that was an intentional change.

> Pretty sure, that was an intentional change.

I think we could make the new breakpoint icon a bit smaller (probably a middle ground between the old size and new size).

This might be regression from #49645
SVG icons have a `viewBox` property defined. Most of them have "0 0 16 16", but e.g. the ruler icon has "0 0 4.2333 4.2333". Changing it to 16 16 doesn't help though, so not sure what is wrong here. Also seems like the property can be dropped (it repeats width and height), it would make the SVGs smaller.

AFAIK they are parsed for different purposes, so viewport values cannot be dropped. It's kind of like a clipping rectangle of the image. But even if they can, let the SVG optimizer do it, no need to edit that out manually.

Probably opening it with a vector editor and correcting the size should work for the issue though. I can do it later, if you want.

> AFAIK they are parsed for different purposes, so viewport values cannot be dropped. It's kind of like a clipping rectangle of the image.

Looks like it corresponds to image (inverted?) scale. If you drop it, it uses a default of 1.

I opened the Ruler.svg in Inkscape and it appears correctly, but indeed it has a scale value modified. When I set it to 1, the icon appears as in the editor. So seems like ThorVG doesn't support document scale? Or it's not enabled for import?
That's something @fire may know, but I don't think there is any reason here for us to use scale anyway. I'd fix the images instead, and worry about ThorVG later, if the need arises.
Can I have the exact link to the `.svg` so I check the online thorvg viewer?

review_comments: Ah nevermind, I see it's connected to `theme_changed` and that gives meaning to the above `TODO`, I guess this plugin doesn't get `NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED`?
Indeed, `EditorPlugin` is not a control and doesn't have it, which is why I had to rely on the signal instead. Decided not to risk with a proper fix here amongst all the other changes.
